answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing or negotiating with them cannot satisfy the objective. Memory c2 documents a prior primary switch to a low-cost vendor that cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing; memory c6 captures the multi-year commitment path that unlocks volume pricing. With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line already at 94% of committed volume, moving primary now preserves the lowest-TCO option while the timing pressure forecloses a dual-source cycle in one round. Verification budget is spent on c6 and c2 because they are the two memories most directly load-bearing for this decision: c2 validates the cost-cut mechanism, c6 supplies the contracting structure needed to sustain the savings without narrowing service scope. Single-source exposure is acknowledged; the line running near capacity means any onboarding disruption translates to delivery risk, and switching primary duplicates that risk into the new vendor rather than distributing it. If verification changes the picture — particularly if c2's cost figures were context-bound or c6's terms came with concessions that erode the savings — the intended action would shift back toward negotiate_terms with the incumbent or defer_decision to allow a two-source design.
